October 15, 2026

Zelensky breaks with Trump as US limits Starlink and withholds strike warnings

tags: war, politics, defence
sources: @aaronparnas

Starlink and Star Shield service in Ukraine was disrupted over a 24-hour period, and Elon Musk said the systems are owned and controlled by the US government, with limits on speed or usage decided by the US military and the president. CBS News reported that the Trump administration may have intentionally withheld early warnings of Russian ballistic missile strikes, which the administration attributed to bad weather; President Zelensky said Kyiv received no advance warning this time. Russia launched more than 850 drones overnight and struck a supermarket in Odessa during rush hour, and Zelensky said strikes on Russian refineries would resume, breaking with Trump. CNBC reported the United States may offer Russia sanctions relief to restart negotiations.

FBI director Kash Patel posts "From Russia with love" amid reported Moscow trip

tags: politics, legal, surveillance
sources: @aaronparnas, @hunteralexanderhowell, @total.hypocrisy, @oafnation_actual

Al Arabiya English reported that FBI Director Kash Patel had landed in Moscow to meet Russian officials, and roughly an hour later the FBI said he was in Virginia rather than Moscow. Patel posted "From Russia, with Love..." on the same day Russian strikes killed Ukrainians and left over 600,000 people without power. The reported counterpart, FSB chief Alexander Bortnikov, has been sanctioned by the United States over the poisoning of Alexei Navalny and over election influence operations. Patel has previously said FBI contact with Russia is limited to transnational crime, and at a September congressional hearing he declined to rule out sending armed federal agents to polling places for the midterms.

Justice Department pursues denaturalization case against Rep. Ilhan Omar

tags: politics, immigration, legal
sources: @aaronparnas, @total.hypocrisy

The Wall Street Journal reported that the Trump administration raided Representative Ilhan Omar's home as part of an effort to build a case to strip her citizenship and deport her. Agents seized her phone, laptop and passport, according to NBC News and other reporting, and subpoenas were issued to people around her. The legal bar for denaturalization is high and no evidence of wrongdoing has been presented; Omar has been a US citizen for decades.

Trump cancels livestream of Fort Hood shooter's execution

tags: politics, legal, defence
sources: @aaronparnas, @carolinegleich, @groundnews, @oafnation_actual

President Trump said the Pentagon will not livestream the December 3 firing squad execution of Nidal Malik Hasan, the former Army major convicted of killing 13 people at Fort Hood in 2009. The reversal followed bipartisan criticism, including from Utah Senator John Curtis, objections from Catholic leaders, and campaigning by VoteVets and Fort Hood survivors who warned the broadcast would aid extremist recruitment. An Economist/YouGov poll found 69% of US adults opposed broadcasting executions, including 52% of Republicans. In announcing the decision, Trump blamed the Obama administration's FBI for a key intelligence failure before the shooting; immediate family members of victims may still attend in person.

September producer price inflation jumps to 6.3%, far above forecasts

tags: markets, economy, politics
sources: @aaronparnas, @carolinegleich

September PPI inflation rose to 6.3%, against economist expectations of 5.3%, and core PPI rose to 5% versus an expected 4.4%. That is the second-highest producer inflation reading since November 2022. The figures raise expectations that the Federal Reserve will move toward rate hikes. A Fox News poll cited alongside the data put approval of the president's handling of inflation at 22% and overall approval at 36%, with prices up almost 4% from a year earlier.

Texas computer glitch delayed more than 600,000 voter registrations

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

The New York Times confirmed that a technical glitch in the Texas registration system delayed more than 600,000 voter registrations ahead of early voting beginning Monday. County officials say many have since been processed and that they are working to ensure registrations are accurate. A voting rights group filed a lawsuit in the past week accusing the state agency responsible and the Secretary of State of failing to maintain a reliable online voter registration system.

Bar complaint filed against White House press secretary Katie Zacharia

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

The watchdog group Campaign for Accountability filed a complaint with the California State Bar alleging that White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia repeatedly held herself out as entitled to practice law without a license, which California treats as a crime. The Wall Street Journal reported that Zacharia took the California bar exam but failed it and has never been licensed. Trump had publicly described her as an attorney; after law school she worked as an international legal consultant in China, a role that does not require bar admission. Zacharia has said the matter is a misunderstanding.

Bank of America fined $1.21 billion over anti-money laundering failures

tags: markets, legal
sources: @groundnews

US regulators fined Bank of America more than $1.21 billion for failing to detect and report potential money laundering and other illicit activity. The Treasury Department said the bank did not report more than $5 billion in suspicious transactions, including $1 billion involving national security risks, and accused it of prioritising revenue over compliance. The package includes a record $750 million penalty from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency and $11.6 million for more than 400 apparent sanctions violations involving payments to countries including Russia and Iran. The bank said it has invested billions in financial crime prevention.

Retired ICE officer describes militarised culture inside the agency

tags: immigration, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

An anonymous retired ICE enforcement officer said in a published interview that newer recruits treat the job as a combat role, criticising the use of rifles and heavy equipment for routine arrests in civilian settings. The officer said Brendan Cuni, identified at the scene of an October 8 shooting in New York City, was already under investigation over other incidents, including dragging a pregnant woman in Minneapolis and allegedly fraudulent administrative arrest warrants. The officer also described promotion based on internal cliques, colleagues arrested for selling drugs and an officer caught stealing from detainees, and said recruits now go straight from the academy into fugitive operations.

RFK Jr. says 189,000 dead or duplicate enrollments removed from subsidised health coverage

tags: health, politics
sources: @groundnews

Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. announced that the federal government removed 189,000 subsidised Medicare, Medicaid and CHIP enrollments linked to deceased individuals or duplicate coverage records. The Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services identified the enrollments in 2026 and eliminated the associated subsidies to prevent payments to insurers, contacting affected individuals or their estates with 30 days to dispute errors. Kennedy projected savings of $738 million in 2026 and $1.5 billion annually thereafter.

Protester demanding Epstein files release assaulted at Trump rally

tags: politics, policing
sources: @hunteralexanderhowell

A protester wearing a shirt calling for the release of the Epstein files was physically assaulted by multiple attendees at a rally. When law enforcement arrived, the protester was detained and escorted out rather than those who carried out the assault. The president referred to the protester from the stage as a paid protester.

Trump says major oil, gas and mineral exploration is coming to Greenland

tags: defence, climate, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

President Trump said that massive oil, gas and mineral exploration is being prepared in Greenland, describing the territory as critical to defending the United States. The announcement follows a September agreement expanding US military access, adding two further defence locations and supporting plans for the Golden Dome missile defence system. No exploration timeline or specific projects were announced.

OpenAI engineer arrested over hidden recording device in executive conference room

tags: surveillance, tech, legal
sources: @oafnation_actual

The FBI arrested Abdulrahman Alfozan, a 35-year-old Saudi engineer at OpenAI, accused of secretly planting an encrypted recording device in an executive conference room. Prosecutors say the recorder was hidden in toilet paper behind a television in a room used for sensitive company and government-related discussions, and that a second device was found in his bag. He faces up to five years in prison if convicted.

Arizona race highlights six House votes against ending the Iran war

tags: politics, war, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

The House has voted six times this year on resolutions directing the president and the defence secretary to end the war in Iran, and Arizona Representative Juan Ciscomani voted against each one. Only six House districts contain more veterans than his. His opponent, Joanna Mendoza, served 20 years in the Navy and Marine Corps, deployed to Iraq and Afghanistan and retired as a gunnery sergeant; she is running as part of a group of women veterans campaigning together. Ciscomani is also criticised for staying silent when the administration announced plans to cut tens of thousands of jobs at the Department of Veterans Affairs.

Utah voters receive ballots as endorsements and amendment fights take shape

tags: politics, climate
sources: @carolinegleich

Ballots for Utah's November 3 general election went out in the mail this week, with a county-by-county endorsement list circulating that includes Democrats, Forward Party candidates and an independent. The guide urges voters to retain all judges except Weber County Justice Court Judge Trent Nelson, whom the state's judicial review panel recommends against retaining. It also urges no votes on Amendment A, which would move notice rules out of the state Constitution and let lawmakers write them, and Amendment B, under which a citizen measure passing with 59% of the vote could still fail. Ballots must arrive by 8 p.m. on November 3 or be placed in a drop box by that time on Election Day.

Republican congressman heckled at town hall over gas prices

tags: politics, economy
sources: @aaronparnas

Representative Andy Harris of Maryland was met with laughter at a town hall after attributing rising diesel prices to Democratic environmental regulations. Harris objected to the interruption, telling a constituent she was being rude and invoking the First Amendment. The exchange came amid broader public anger over fuel costs.

Appeals court rules old DUI conviction does not strip gun rights

tags: legal, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

A federal appeals court ruled that a decades-old DUI conviction did not justify permanently barring a Pennsylvania man from owning firearms. In a separate case, the same court upheld a firearm ban against a man convicted of making violent threats.

Military retirement COLA set at 3.6% for 2027

tags: defence, economy
sources: @oafnation_actual

The 2027 military retirement cost-of-living adjustment has been set at 3.6%, up from 2.8% this year, following the latest inflation report. A matching increase to VA disability compensation is expected, pending congressional approval.

Army suspends hometown recruiting program

tags: defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

The Army has suspended its 14-day hometown recruiting program. Leaders said soldiers participating in it were not spending enough time assisting recruiters.
